from solution import cal_sum
import inspect
import solution


def test_issue_example_9():
    """Example asserts cal_sum(9) == 49."""
    assert cal_sum(9) == 49  # 3+0+2+3+2+5+5+7+10+12 = 49


def test_issue_zero():
    """Sum of perrin numbers up to n=0 is 3."""
    assert cal_sum(0) == 3  # P0 = 3, so 3 = 3


def test_issue_one():
    """Sum of perrin numbers up to n=1 is 3."""
    assert cal_sum(1) == 3  # 3+0 = 3


def test_issue_two():
    """Sum of perrin numbers up to n=2 is 5."""
    assert cal_sum(2) == 5  # 3+0+2 = 5


def test_issue_three():
    """Sum of perrin numbers up to n=3 is 8."""
    assert cal_sum(3) == 8  # 3+0+2+3 = 8


def test_issue_five():
    """Sum of perrin numbers up to n=5 is 15."""
    assert cal_sum(5) == 15  # 3+0+2+3+2+5 = 15


def test_issue_eight():
    """Sum of perrin numbers up to n=8 just below example is 37."""
    assert cal_sum(8) == 37  # 3+0+2+3+2+5+5+7+10 = 37


def test_issue_ten():
    """Sum of perrin numbers up to n=10 just above example is 66."""
    assert cal_sum(10) == 66  # 3+0+2+3+2+5+5+7+10+12+17 = 66


def test_issue_twelve():
    """Sum of perrin numbers up to larger n=12 is 117."""
    assert cal_sum(12) == 117  # 3+0+2+3+2+5+5+7+10+12+17+22+29 = 117


def test_contract_callable():
    """Public interface shows module solution defines cal_sum."""
    assert callable(solution.cal_sum)


def test_contract_single_parameter():
    """Public interface shows def cal_sum(n) with one parameter."""
    assert len(inspect.signature(cal_sum).parameters) == 1  # one parameter: n
